key_insight: An open-source toolkit automates RHEED control and analysis so both researchers and AI agents can guide thin-film growth with less manual intervention.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the barrier to autonomous, quantitative monitoring of pulsed-laser-deposition processes and makes RHEED workflows more interoperable, extensible, and agent-ready.
method: Programmable electron-optics control with automated beam alignment and rocking-curve acquisition
Training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment for faster setup
Shared GUI/API access via auto RHEED plus an MCP server and extensible adapter interface for new analysis and simulation methods
evidence_signal: The toolkit was demonstrated on a pulsed laser deposition system, including an agent-driven workflow that used natural-language requests to select, configure, and run quantitative analyses.
watch_item: Practical adoption will depend on robust integration with diverse hardware setups and on the reliability of newly added community analysis or simulation adapters.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
